key_insight: HySTAR stabilizes credit assignment in cooperative MARL by fixing an anchored hypergraph decomposition scaffold while letting representations adapt over time.
engineering_relevance: The method is relevant for engineering teams building scalable multi-agent controllers because it improves robustness to changing interactions, partial observability, and agent turnover.
method: Anchors a sparse overlapping hypergraph to keep the value decomposition topology temporally consistent.
Uses a spatiotemporal encoder to capture physical and task-dependent agent interactions.
Combines temporal and structural relevance to produce agent-specific advantages from shared rewards.
evidence_signal: Across SMAC, GRF, Traffic Junction, and MPE, HySTAR outperforms MAPPO-style, value-factorization, and dynamic-grouping baselines, with up to 16.7% gain over MAPPO on hard SMAC and up to 40.2% faster convergence on Traffic Junction.
watch_item: Anchoring the decomposition scaffold may reduce flexibility if the true interaction structure changes rapidly, so topology design and hyperparameters need careful tuning.
paper_title: HySTAR: Anchored Hypergraphs for Stable Credit Assignment in Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
